question: Should ClawSweeper adopt a seven-day cross-route ingress-receipt protocol and require target repositories to opt into the documented dispatcher fingerprint after the per-item queue protocol is settled?
rationale: The patch introduces a durable admission contract across two independently operated delivery routes; choosing the identity field set, retention period, rollout sequence, and acceptable missed-review risk is a product and operational policy decision rather than a mechanical code correction.

options.title: Approve a gated canary after queue sequencing
options.body: Approve the v1 identity envelope and seven-day retention only after the related queue direction is accepted, then require the full paired-route canary on a rebased branch.

options.title: Keep both routes independently admitted
options.body: Decline coalescing and retain the current redundant but independently reliable exact-review delivery behavior.

options.title: Request a narrower design
options.body: Ask for a proposal that proves the same-event relation with a different receipt scope or rollout boundary before accepting durable coalescing.

recommendation.title: Approve a gated canary after queue sequencing
recommendation.body: Approve the v1 identity envelope and seven-day retention only after the related queue direction is accepted, then require the full paired-route canary on a rebased branch.
